Documentation → Administration → Settings → Clone / Migrate

Clone / Migrate settings

Fleet-wide defaults for the Server Policy Clone and Migrate dialogs — the dummy-IP rules that keep a copied VIP from taking real traffic, the fallback dummy IP, and whether the Web Protection Profile is copied by default.

👤 ForAdministratorOperator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereSettings → Fleet & Devices → Clone / Migrate (URL /settings/#tab-clonerules)

  • "Clone/Migrate rules NOT saved: match '…' and replace '…' must have the same octet count"

What is it?#

Clone / Migrate holds the defaults the Server Policy Clone and Migrate dialogs start from. A bulk clone or migrate always rewrites each copy's VIP to a dummy IP using these rules, so the copy cannot take real traffic; a single-policy dialog prefills the same suggestion but lets the operator decide. How cloning works is described in Policy cloning.

What does it do?#

  • Dummy-IP transformation rules — ordered rules that replace the leading octets of the source VIP and keep the rest (first match wins). 10 → 240 turns {ip} into 240.1.10.1.
  • Fallback dummy IP — used when no rule matches (or the source is not parseable).
  • Copy the Web Protection Profile by default on clone / migrate — the default for the dialog's WPP choice. Operators see these values in the dialog and can override them per run only after ticking Override admin defaults.

Requirements#

  • users.manage to edit.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

POST /settings/clone-rules requires users.manage; others get 403 and do not see the tab. Operators running a clone see the values read-only unless they tick Override admin defaults.

How to use#

  1. Open Settings → Fleet & Devices → Clone / Migrate.
  2. Edit the rules under Dummy-IP transformation rules (first match wins); two empty rows are offered for new rules. Clear both cells of a row to remove it.
  3. Set Fallback dummy IP (no rule matches).
  4. Tick or untick Copy the Web Protection Profile by default on clone / migrate.
  5. Click Save clone/migrate rules — "Clone/Migrate rules saved (N IP rules)."

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
IP starts with (octets) 1–3 leading octets, each 0–255. Per rule 10
Replace with Same number of octets as the match, each 0–255. Per rule 240
Fallback dummy IP (no rule matches) A valid IPv4 address. Blank saves the default 203.0.113.9. No 203.0.113.9
Copy the Web Protection Profile by default on clone / migrate Default on. No on

Shipped default rules: 10 → 240 and 162 → 241.

Example#

🧪Example — Rewrite two private ranges

Rules: 10 → 240, 172.16 → 240.16. A bulk migration of a policy on VIP {ip} creates the copy on 240.16.4.20; a VIP 192.0.2.80 matches no rule and the copy gets the fallback 203.0.113.9.

Result#

  • The policy is stored in app_settings (clone.rules); audit entry settings.clone_rules with rule count, fallback and WPP default.
  • The next Clone or Migrate dialog shows the new defaults.

Troubleshooting#

"Clone/Migrate rules NOT saved: match '…' and replace '…' must have the same octet count"#

Solution — use the same number of octets on both sides (for example 172.16 → 240.16).

"Clone/Migrate rules NOT saved: a rule matches 1 to 3 leading octets, got '…'"#

Solution — a rule cannot match a full four-octet address; use at most three octets.

"Clone/Migrate rules NOT saved: octet '…' is not in 0-255"#

Solution — correct the octet.

"Clone/Migrate rules NOT saved: fallback IP '…' is not a valid IPv4 address"#

Solution — enter a dotted IPv4 address. Nothing is saved while any error remains; all errors are listed together.

Advanced#

Advanced Notes
  • Rules are evaluated in the order shown; the first rule whose octets prefix the source VIP wins.
  • Leading and trailing dots in a rule are ignored (10. equals 10).
